transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-25
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Liam Park (Redwood Solutions), Jordan Blake (Meridian Head of Data), Priya Patel (Meridian CTO), Alex Nguyen (Meridian SRE), Samir Rao (Meridian Product)

Summary: quick POC scoping focused on cost modeling/unit economics for search/rerank and chat use cases. Discussed tokens per request, batching/caching knobs, budget constraints, and timeline for benchmarks. Decided next steps to exchange workload traces and run an initial benchmark week of 7/6.

Topics: success criteria, workload sizing, sample RPS/QPS, per-token estimates, batching and KV cache impact, dedicated vs hosted cost tradeoffs, timeline and compliance asks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros — I think we all know each other but we'll do a short round.
[00:12] Jordan: Jordan, Head of Data at Meridian. We run recommender and search for ~700 stores and our ecomm site.
[00:18] Priya: Priya, CTO. I'm here for security and budget sign-off.
[00:23] Alex: Alex, SRE; I'll be running any bench s and helping with infra.
[00:27] Maya: Great. Daniel, Liam from Redwood?
[00:30] Daniel: yeah Daniel Ortiz, SE. we focus on perf/benchmarks.
[00:34] Liam: Liam Park, solutions — I'll help map pricing to expected spend.
[00:38] Samir: Samir, product, mostly to align success criteria.
[00:42] Maya: Awesome. Quick agenda: confirm POC goals, walk through expected workloads, discuss cost model levers (batching, kv cache, quantization), and agree logistics/timeline.
[01:00] Jordan: Our main goal is to validate economics: can we run personalization + chat assistants for customer support within our existing cloud budget. Key success metric is below $0.0008 per user query on average for search/rerank, and sub-300ms P50 for interactive chat responses.
[01:25] Priya: Also we need to ensure auditability — SOC2 compliance and KMS integration are must-haves. On-prem maybe later but for POC hosted is preferred.
[01:38] Daniel: ok good. When you say per user query, is that average across short search queries and longer chat sessions? we should split workload classes.
[01:47] Jordan: yes split — roughly 70% short search/rerank (~20-40 tokens generated per request), 20% personalization/context (100-300 tokens), 10% chat sessions (400-1200 tokens avg per session but interactive multi-turn).
[02:07] Maya: that's super helpful. Alex, what QPS are you seeing at peak for these endpoints today?
[02:13] Alex: peak QPS around 120 across geos for search, sustained 30 QPS for personalization, chat is bursty — maybe 10 concurrent active sessions but each session issues multiple calls.
[02:22] Samir: For the POC we can scope to a target 30 QPS aggregate to validate economics; we don't need full production scale.
[02:29] Daniel: Great — that makes batching/caching decisions easier to model. Quick clarification: are you more concerned about latency SLOs or raw cost? there's usually a tradeoff.
[02:38] Priya: both. latency requirement for chat is rigid (P50 < 300ms), search can tolerate up to 500ms. Cost target is the blocker.
[02:47] Liam: ok, I'll outline the typical knobs: model selection (smaller vs larger), batching window/target batch size, KV or prefix cache hit rate, quantization (4/8-bit), and hosting mode (hosted multi-tenant vs dedicated reserved GPUs). each affects per-token compute and cost.
[03:05] Daniel: i'll add that runtime optimizations like continuous batching and request coalescing can give you 2-4x throughput improvement for real-time workloads, but latency tail depends on batch formation timers.
[03:19] Jordan: can you give a back-of-envelope per-token cost? ballpark — we need a initial sanity check.
[03:26] Liam: sure. for hosted with mid-sized open model (approx 13B equivalent if optimized/quantized) — typical per-inference token compute cost range is $0.000002 to $0.00001 per token depending on batch and cache. so for a 30-token request cost might be $0.00006 to $0.0003. with caching and prefix reuse that can drop significantly for repeated prefixes.
[03:53] Priya: those ranges are wide; how do we narrow to our workload?
[03:58] Daniel: we need the actual token distributions — which Jordan said they'd provide. once we run a 72h trace through our benchmarking harness we'll estimate effective batch sizes and cache hit rates, then produce per-token effective cost.
[04:12] Alex: what's the difference in dollars between hosted and dedicated for us? we want to know break-even for committed spend.
[04:18] Liam: dedicated is cheaper per-token at scale but you pay for reserved capacity. example: dedicated reserved pool (8x A100-ish equivalent) might get you to $0.0000015 per token with good batching, but you'd need to commit to monthly spend (e.g., $XXk). hosted is pay-as-you-go with higher per-token but no commit. we will put actual numbers in the pricing sheet.
[04:39] Jordan: For scope of POC let's model three configs: hosted baseline, small dedicated pool, and a mixed policy (hosted failover + dedicated primary).
[04:48] Maya: good. success criteria proposed: 1) Cost projection aligns < 10% of target ($0.0008 per query), 2) Latency SLOs met in benchmark (search P95 <500ms, chat P50 <300ms), 3) Integration checklist passed (KMS, SSO, audit logs). Agree?
[05:06] Priya: yes please add security gating and data residency notes.
[05:10] Daniel: noted. on the benchmarking side we typically run token-level tracing and then simulate different batching configs. we'll run with a few model variants (quantized 4-bit 13B, 8-bit 20B, and a smaller 6B) to show cost/latency curve.
[05:27] Samir: how long to get meaningful numbers?
[05:30] Daniel: if we have traces, we can spin up tests within 48 hours and run 72h traces — but for POC we'll do an initial 24-48h focused run then a longer 72h run if needed.
[05:41] Jordan: timeline wise Meridian wants decision by end of July; can we get POC complete and a recommended config by then?
[05:47] Maya: yes that's feasible: milestone: workload artifacts by 6/30, initial bench run by 7/6, internal review 7/10, recommended config + pricing by 7/17, exec review 7/24.
[05:59] Priya: that timeline works if the pricing looks good.
[06:03] Alex: technical question: how does Redwood's KV cache hit rate work for personalization? we often send user history as prefix; if cache hits then we avoid recomputing the prefix.
[06:12] Daniel: correct — prefix KV caching stores key/value states for recent prefixes. hit rates depend on session stickiness and prefix reuse; for ecommerce personalization with repeated templates you can see 30-60% effective reduction in decoder compute for subsequent tokens. we'll model low/med/high hit rate scenarios.
[06:28] Jordan: and batching windows — what's the impact if we set tight latency timers?
[06:32] Daniel: tighter timers reduce average batch size so per-token compute cost increases; the platform can do dynamic batching so during peaks you get larger batches but tails still matter. we can show curves: batch timer 5ms vs 20ms.
[06:43] Maya: any security red flags for hosted? Priya?
[06:46] Priya: need to confirm KMS, customer-managed keys, audit logs retention, SSO & role-based access, and whether data at rest encryption meets our policy. we also want to see SOC2 report.
[06:58] Liam: we'll include SOC2, ISO docs, and an optional KMS integration design.
[07:02] Samir: pricing sheet — please include a worked example with our traffic profile and show sensitivity to 3 variables: batch size, cache hit rate, and model family.
[07:11] Liam: yes, we'll produce a sensitivity table and a recommended sweet spot.
[07:15] Jordan: are there any hidden infra costs? networking? egress?
[07:20] Liam: depending on deployment egress will be billed by cloud provider; Redwood hosted includes typical network costs in the quote but large media payloads may have additional charges. we'll call out any assumptions.
[07:31] Priya: Regarding on-prem/private — for our compliance group it's more about long-term, not for POC. but we want to understand the delta in ops and unit economics.
[07:40] Daniel: on-prem adds ops overhead; unit compute cost may be lower per-token but you must amortize hardware + staff. we'll put an example TCO with 1yr amortization.
[07:52] Alex: For benchmarks, what do you need from us exactly?
[07:55] Daniel: ideally: (1) three 72h traces of production traffic (anonymized), (2) top 50 prompts for personalization/search, (3) representative session traces for chat, (4) any latency SLOs and error patterns. we gave a short template we'll share.
[08:10] Jordan: we'll get that to you by EoM.
[08:14] Maya: ok. let's talk about concrete numbers — run a hypothetical for one search request (30 tokens) and one chat turn (500 tokens) across three settings: hosted small batch, dedicated small pool with batching, and dedicated with high batching + KV cache.
[08:31] Liam: hosted small batch: assume average batch size 2-3, per-token compute $0.000007 => search 30 tokens = $0.00021, chat 500 tokens = $0.0035.
[08:42] Liam: dedicated small pool: better batch size 8-12, per-token compute $0.0000025 => search 30 = $0.000075, chat 500 = $0.00125.
[08:52] Liam: dedicated + caching: effective token compute reduced 30% for personalization and 10-20% for chat depending on prefix reuse => search could drop to $0.00005, chat to ~$0.001.
[09:03] Priya: so with our mix (70% small search, 20% personalization, 10% chat) what's blended cost per user query?
[09:10] Liam: quick calc: using dedicated small pool numbers weighted: search 70% * $0.000075, personalization (assume 150 tokens avg) cost ~0.000375 * 20% = 0.000075, chat 10% * 0.00125 = 0.000125 => total ~0.000275 per request. that's still above your $0.0008 target? actually below — Jordan check math.
[09:34] Jordan: our target was $0.0008 per user query. 0.000275 seems well under - are we comparing same definitions?
[09:41] Samir: I think our target was $0.0008 per query including any orchestration overhead and network costs; so 0.000275 leaves room. good sign.
[09:50] Daniel: keep in mind these are optimistic if caching/batching hit. worst-case hosted numbers could be 2-3x higher.
[09:58] Maya: good to call out sensitivity. We'll deliver a sensitivity matrix.
[10:02] Jordan: what about cold-start and multi-turn chat where KV cache can't help?
[10:07] Daniel: multi-turn benefits more as the session progresses; cold starts will be costlier but you amortize across session. we will model session-level amortization in the benchmark.
[10:18] Priya: for compliance — can Redwood support customer-managed keys in hosted?
[10:22] Liam: yes, we support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys for encryption at rest; we'll send the integration doc.
[10:29] Alex: any recommended models? small ops teams like ours prefer not to tune too much; a 13B optimized quantized model might be sweet spot.
[10:36] Daniel: agree — 13B quantized 4-bit often a good latency/cost compromise; we will show 6B/13B/20B comparisons.
[10:44] Samir: what's the expected CPU/infra footprint if we go dedicated? I mean additional infra for orchestration and autoscaling.
[10:51] Liam: dedicated includes orchestration and autoscaling. you'll still need some peering/VPC setup; we'll estimate the required GPU count based on your 30 QPS test target. likely small pool (2-4 GPUs) for the POC.
[11:03] Jordan: can you provide the break-even committed spend for dedicated?
[11:06] Liam: yes we'll model break-even at multiple commit levels; initial guess for your profile might be $8-12k/month for meaningful cost advantage vs hosted. exacts in the sheet.
[11:18] Priya: okay. any other risks? data residency?
[11:21] Maya: we flagged that — Redwood private/on-prem is an option but out of scope for POC. we'll note the migration path.
[11:28] Jordan: final question — can we run a small smoke test with sample traces on hosted first? to verify integration and basic latency numbers.
[11:35] Daniel: yes absolutely. if you can supply sample traces (anonymized) we can run a quick hosted smoke test within 48 hours and share results.
[11:45] Maya: Great. Let's recap action items and timeline.
[11:48] Maya: Redwood to send pricing + benchmark template (Maya/Liam/Daniel).
[11:52] Jordan: Meridian to provide traces and prompts by 6/30.
[11:56] Daniel: SE will run initial smoke test and then 72h benchmark once we have traces.
[12:01] Priya: We'll review compliance docs and come back with any gating items by 7/2.
[12:06] Maya: And we'll plan the deep-dive week of 7/6.
[12:10] Jordan: sounds good.
[12:12] Maya: thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with the sheet and meeting notes.
[12:18] (call ends)

Notes on transcription quality: some words may be garbled, product names abbreviated; speakers may cut over.
